source: JZ Mock D · Paper 1 · Question 13 · Publisher worked solution
knowledgePattern: Compose off-axis reflections and input changes in order

hints.title: Keep a line for each change
hints.body: First do the horizontal changes II to V to y=sinx. You may leave reflection I until the end because it changes only the height.
hints.recap: A horizontal stretch by factor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> replaces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>.
hints.pitfall: In a shift to the left, the change inside the function has a plus sign.
hints.pause: Write the equation after II, then after III, without skipping a line.

recall.reminder: A horizontal stretch by factor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> replaces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>.

hints.title: Check the two vertical mirror lines
hints.body: For IV, replace x by −x. For V, check whether the resulting sine curve is already symmetric about the stated line: a vertical line through a sine maximum or minimum is a mirror line.
hints.recap: Reflecting in a line of symmetry leaves a graph unchanged.
hints.pitfall: A vertical mirror line changes horizontal positions, not heights.
hints.pause: Locate the maxima and minima of your current sine curve and decide what V does.

recall.reminder: A reflection moves points across the mirror line by equal distances; a graph symmetric about that line stays in place.

hints.title: Do the height reflection last
hints.body: For reflection I, a height y moves to 2(−3)−y. Apply this to the equation you have after the horizontal changes.
hints.recap: To reflect a height in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>, replace it by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.pitfall: Apply the minus sign to the whole current function.
hints.pause: Simplify the sine expression and match the resulting equation to an option.

recall.reminder: To reflect a height in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>, replace it by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math>.

solution:
1. Work on the horizontal changes. Reflection I changes only the height, so it can be done last. The stretch II and left shift III turn the curve into y=sin(x/2+π/6).

2. Apply the first horizontal reflection. IV replaces x by −x, giving y=sin(−x/2+π/6). At x=4π/3, the angle is −π/2, so this point is a minimum. The vertical line through a sine minimum is a line of symmetry. Thus V leaves this curve unchanged.

3. Reflect the heights. Reflection in y=−3 sends a height y to −6−y. We therefore obtain y=−6−sin(−x/2+π/6)=−6+sin(x/2−π/6), using sin(−t)=−sint. Answer C.
